_comment: Coral projection player — copy to coral-projection.json and edit. Mirrors config.yaml's role for the server: every port, path and timing lives here, never in code.
_video_dir_note: Resolved against THIS FILE's directory, not the process working directory. "video" gives the portable layout — CoralProjection.app, coral-projection.json and video/ side by side — so the whole bundle works wherever it is copied, including onto the cold-restore USB. An absolute path also works for bench use, but breaks portability.
_clips_note: ProRes 422, 2560x800, 30fps, bt709-tagged. Three loops plus one one-shot. healthy/fluorescent/bleached loop forever and their lengths do not affect behaviour — longer just means a rarer wrap. Push healthy longest: it is the idle state, on screen between visitors and therefore most of the exhibition. bleached wants length too, since an abandoned bleach holds at full opacity for ~3 minutes (idle_timeout_s 180 + recovery_lag_s 30). fluorescent can be shortest — state 1 is a blend, so its wrap is half-masked by the healthy layer. latch plays once on the 1->2 bleach latch; its bound is crossfade_s < length < recovery_lag_s (1.5s < 21s < 30s), because state 2 can never be shorter than recovery_lag_s, so a clip under that can never be cut short mid-telling. Do not lower recovery_lag_s below ~25s without shortening the latch clip. There are no directional transition clips; every other change is an opacity blend driven by intensity.
_loop_note: The three hold clips MUST have closed loop points — their tail cross-dissolved onto their head — or they visibly jump at every wrap, forever, in a quiet gallery. Cutting them straight out of a continuous master does NOT close them. tools/loop_seam.py does it and measures the wrap discontinuity before and after, so the fix is verified rather than assumed. The clip comes back one overlap shorter than it went in.
_crossfade_note: One fade rate for everything. Also acts as the slew limit on the state 0/1 intensity blend, and as the lead-in used to hand a one-shot over before its last frame (so the clip never freezes while fading).
_video_size_note: Native frame size of the exported clips — same as the canvas, so every source pixel maps to one projector pixel. Stated, not detected: the RenderTextures are built before any clip is prepared, and a RenderTexture whose aspect disagrees with the video squashes the frame before the compositor sees it. The player logs a warning at startup if a prepared clip disagrees with these numbers.
_display_note: Spanned canvas across both Epson EB-435W (1280x800 each). macOS Displays must be set to Extend, arranged side by side — that is an OS setting, not something this player controls.
_fit_note: With source and canvas both 2560x800 this is a no-op (scale 1,1 offset 0,0) and pan is irrelevant. It stays as a safety net: if a clip is ever exported at the wrong size, 'cover' crops to fill without distorting rather than silently squashing. Watch for the startup warning instead of relying on it.
